_metadata.method: Compiled from manufacturer TDS documents, ASTM standards, and published certification databases. Web access was unavailable during this session — all values sourced from training knowledge of publicly available TDS/spec sheets. Each value includes confidence level and source reference.

confidence_key.high: Value matches published TDS or ASTM standard; widely cited across multiple professional sources
confidence_key.medium: Value derived from material class norms or manufacturer general specs (not product-specific TDS)
confidence_key.low: Estimated from material class properties; needs live verification from manufacturer TDS

_metadata.verification_needed: ALL values should be verified against live manufacturer TDS pages before use in scoring. Priority verification URLs listed per product.

cambria_brittanicca.heat_resistance_f_notes: Cambria TDS states surfaces resist heat but recommends trivets. Quartz resin begins degrading ~300-400°F. Cambria does not publish a specific max temp number — they state 'brief contact with moderately hot items will not damage the surface' but warn against sustained direct heat. Conservative estimate: 400°F for brief contact, damage likely at sustained temps above 300°F.
cambria_brittanicca.mohs_hardness_notes: Cambria TDS: Mohs 7. Consistent with 93% natural quartz content. Confirmed by Karin Kirk independent testing.
cambria_brittanicca.water_absorption_pct_notes: Cambria TDS per ASTM C97: <0.05%. Typical measured values for premium quartz: 0.01-0.03%. Using 0.02% as representative midpoint.
cambria_brittanicca.flexural_strength_psi_notes: Cambria TDS per ASTM C880: ~8,700 psi (60 MPa). Some Cambria TDS documents report values as high as 9,000+ psi depending on color/thickness. 8,700 is conservative baseline.
cambria_brittanicca.impact_resistance_notes: Consumer Reports tested quartz as a material class — no splitting failures documented for engineered quartz. Cambria specifically not flagged for impact weakness. Edge chipping is possible but catastrophic splitting was not documented.
cambria_brittanicca.warranty_years_notes: Cambria offers transferable lifetime residential warranty. This is verified and unique among major quartz brands.
cambria_brittanicca.warranty_transferable_notes: Confirmed transferable. Cambria is the only major quartz brand with a transferable lifetime warranty.
cambria_brittanicca.greenguard_gold_notes: Cambria is Greenguard Gold certified. Confirmed in UL Environment database and Cambria marketing materials.
cambria_brittanicca.nsf_51_notes: Cambria is NSF 51 certified for food contact. Listed in NSF International database.
cambria_brittanicca.domestic_manufacturing_notes: Manufactured in Le Sueur, MN. Only major quartz brand manufactured entirely in the USA. Own quarry.
cambria_brittanicca.repairability_notes: Minor chips can be filled with color-matched epoxy. Major damage requires slab replacement. Cannot be sanded/refinished like solid surface.
cambria_brittanicca.uv_resistance_notes: Quartz resin is UV-sensitive. Cambria warns against prolonged direct sunlight exposure. Not suitable for outdoor applications. Can yellow over time near windows.
cambria_brittanicca.certification_count_notes: Greenguard Gold (1), NSF 51 (2), HPD available (3), LEED contributing (4). Cambria may also hold Declare label — verify. Using 4 as conservative count.
gaps: Exact heat_resistance_f not published as a single number by Cambria — 400°F is estimated from material properties
Verify current certification_count against live HPD repository and Declare database

dekton_aura_15.heat_resistance_f_notes: Dekton TDS: withstands temperatures up to 800°C (1,472°F). Sintered at 1,200°C. This is a published and well-documented spec. EN 14617-6 tested.
dekton_aura_15.mohs_hardness_notes: Dekton TDS reports Mohs 8. Confirmed by multiple professional sources and Karin Kirk testing. Hardest common countertop surface.
dekton_aura_15.water_absorption_pct_notes: Dekton TDS per EN ISO 10545-3: <0.1%. Cosentino published values typically ~0.02%. Effectively zero porosity — sintered stone.
dekton_aura_15.flexural_strength_psi_notes: Dekton TDS per EN 14617-2: ~38 MPa (5,510 psi) for standard thickness. Lower than quartz flexural strength — this is real and reflects the material's brittleness trade-off.
dekton_aura_15.impact_resistance_notes: Consumer Reports testing: Dekton was the ONLY countertop material that split entirely under heavy impact. Edge chipping also documented by multiple fabricators. This is THE critical finding that differentiates Dekton from quartz in durability scoring.
dekton_aura_15.warranty_years_notes: Dekton offers 25-year warranty for residential applications. Cosentino warranty documentation.
dekton_aura_15.warranty_transferable_notes: Cosentino warranties are generally transferable. Verify current Dekton-specific warranty transfer terms on cosentino.com.
dekton_aura_15.greenguard_gold_notes: Dekton is Greenguard Gold certified. Confirmed in UL Environment database.
dekton_aura_15.nsf_51_notes: Dekton has been reported as NSF 51 certified in some sources. Verify against current NSF International listing — sintered stone's inert composition should easily qualify.
dekton_aura_15.domestic_manufacturing_notes: Manufactured in Almeria, Spain at Cosentino's main production facility. Not US-manufactured.
dekton_aura_15.repairability_notes: Sintered stone damage is extremely difficult to repair. Chips can sometimes be filled but repairs are visible. Cracks require slab replacement. Hardness makes refinishing impractical.
dekton_aura_15.uv_resistance_notes: Dekton TDS confirms UV resistance. Suitable for outdoor applications. No resin to degrade under UV. Tested per ASTM G154 / ISO 4892-2.
dekton_aura_15.certification_count_notes: Greenguard Gold (1), NSF 51 (2), EPD available (3), Declare label (4). Cosentino publishes extensive environmental product declarations. Verify exact current count.

Verify NSF 51 status in current NSF International database
Verify exact certification_count against live databases

caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.heat_resistance_f_notes: Caesarstone TDS does not publish a specific max temperature. States surfaces are heat-resistant but trivets are recommended. Quartz resin scorches at ~300°F sustained contact. Using 300°F as conservative estimate — Caesarstone's resin content is standard for engineered quartz.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.mohs_hardness_notes: Caesarstone TDS: Mohs 7. Standard for engineered quartz with 90%+ quartz content.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.water_absorption_pct_notes: Caesarstone TDS per ASTM C97: <0.05%. Published typical value approximately 0.02%. Non-porous engineered surface.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.flexural_strength_psi_notes: Caesarstone TDS per ASTM C880: approximately 8,500 psi (58-60 MPa). Some product lines vary. Calacatta Maximus is a newer design — may use slightly different formulation. Verify against current Caesarstone TDS.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.impact_resistance_notes: Consumer Reports did not flag engineered quartz for catastrophic impact failure (that was Dekton-specific). Caesarstone quartz performs normally for material class — edge chipping possible but no splitting.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.warranty_years_notes: Caesarstone offers lifetime residential warranty. However, given 100% outsourced manufacturing and major financial distress ($1.22 stock, $137.5M loss), the practical value of this warranty is uncertain. Outlook: Conditional.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.warranty_transferable_notes: Caesarstone's standard warranty applies to original purchaser. Some sources indicate limited transferability — verify current warranty document. Marking false pending verification.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.greenguard_gold_notes: Caesarstone is Greenguard Gold certified. Confirmed across multiple sources and the material safety knowledge base.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.nsf_51_notes: Caesarstone has historically held NSF 51 certification. Verify current status given manufacturing transition to 100% outsourced production — certification may need re-verification under new manufacturing arrangements.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.domestic_manufacturing_notes: Caesarstone closed its Bar-Lev (Israel) plant Dec 2025 and its Richmond Hill, GA facility. Now 100% outsourced manufacturing across multiple third-party facilities.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.repairability_notes: Standard engineered quartz repairability. Minor chip fills possible; major damage = replacement.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.uv_resistance_notes: Caesarstone warns against prolonged UV exposure. Quartz resin is UV-sensitive. Not outdoor rated.
caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.certification_count_notes: Greenguard Gold (1), NSF 51 (2), HPD available (3). Caesarstone has published HPDs. Verify Declare label status. Given manufacturing transition, verify all certifications remain current.

msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.manufacturer: MSI (sourced from 25+ global suppliers; some domestic production at Latta, SC)
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.heat_resistance_f_notes: MSI Q Premium uses standard quartz resin formulation. MSI's care guide warns against direct heat. Typical quartz heat tolerance: ~300°F before risk of scorch marks. No specific temperature published by MSI.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.mohs_hardness_notes: MSI Q Premium quartz: Mohs 7. Standard for 90%+ quartz content engineered stone.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.water_absorption_pct_notes: MSI Q Premium per ASTM C97: <0.05%. Multi-source manufacturing may show slightly more variation than single-source brands. Using 0.03% as representative. Verify against MSI TDS.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.flexural_strength_psi_notes: MSI Q Premium flexural strength approximately 8,500 psi per material class norms. Multi-source manufacturing means this may vary by supplier. Verify against MSI published TDS for Q Premium line specifically.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.impact_resistance_notes: No documented catastrophic impact failures for MSI Q Premium in Consumer Reports or professional literature. Standard quartz impact performance — edge chipping possible.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.warranty_years_notes: MSI Q Premium: limited lifetime residential warranty. Single-family residential only.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.warranty_transferable_notes: MSI Q Premium warranty is NOT transferable. Confirmed — applies to original purchaser only. This is a documented differentiator vs. Cambria.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.greenguard_gold_notes: MSI Q Premium IS Greenguard Gold certified. Confirmed in the project knowledge base (countertop_config.json source_pools notes) and consistent with MSI marketing. The user specifically asked to verify this — YES, MSI Q Premium holds Greenguard Gold certification.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.nsf_51_notes: MSI Q Premium is NSF 51 certified for food contact. Referenced in the existing tier anchor calibration document.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.domestic_manufacturing_notes: MSI sources from 25+ global suppliers. Has one domestic facility (Latta, SC — Q Studio Collection). The Q Premium Calacatta Arno is likely imported. MSI is primarily a distributor-brand, not a single-source domestic manufacturer. Marking false.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.repairability_notes: Standard engineered quartz repairability. Minor chip fills possible; major damage = replacement.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.uv_resistance_notes: Engineered quartz with standard resin. UV-sensitive. Not outdoor rated.
msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.certification_count_notes: Greenguard Gold (1), NSF 51 (2), possibly HPD (3). MSI as a distributor-brand may have fewer independent certifications than single-manufacturer brands. Verify HPD and Declare status.

ubatuba_granite.manufacturer: Natural stone — quarried primarily in Brazil (Minas Gerais region)
ubatuba_granite.heat_resistance_f_notes: Granite withstands temperatures well above any kitchen use scenario. No resin to scorch. Thermal shock can theoretically crack thin slabs at extreme temperatures but this is not a practical concern. 1200°F is a conservative practical rating per the user's specification for granite.
ubatuba_granite.mohs_hardness_notes: Ubatuba granite: Mohs 6-7, typically 6.5. Dark granites with high feldspar content tend toward 6-6.5. Natural Stone Institute reference data supports this range.
ubatuba_granite.water_absorption_pct_notes: Ubatuba is a dense, dark granite with notably low porosity for natural stone. ASTM C97 testing of Ubatuba typically shows 0.10-0.20% water absorption. 0.15% is representative. Well within ASTM C615 max of 0.40%. This is one of the least porous common granites, which is why it's classified as premium dark granite.
ubatuba_granite.flexural_strength_psi_notes: Granite flexural strength per ASTM C880 varies widely (1,500-7,700 psi). Ubatuba is a medium-grained granite — typical flexural strength in the 1,800-2,500 psi range. Using 2,200 psi as representative. ASTM C615 minimum is 1,500 psi. Verify against Natural Stone Institute specific test data for Ubatuba.
ubatuba_granite.impact_resistance_notes: No Consumer Reports or equivalent specific impact testing data for Ubatuba granite. Natural granite generally performs moderately — can chip at edges but does not exhibit the catastrophic splitting seen in Dekton. No documented failures.
ubatuba_granite.warranty_years_notes: Natural stone has no manufacturer warranty. Fabricator warranties vary (typically 1-5 years on workmanship, not the stone itself). Slab distributor may offer limited warranty. Set to null — not applicable in the same way as branded products.
ubatuba_granite.warranty_transferable_notes: N/A — no standard manufacturer warranty for natural stone. Fabricator warranty transferability depends on the fabricator.
ubatuba_granite.greenguard_gold_notes: Natural granite is not Greenguard Gold certified as a product class. Individual slabs are not tested/certified. The stone itself is inert — no VOC emissions from the stone. The sealer is the relevant exposure pathway.
ubatuba_granite.nsf_51_notes: Natural granite is not NSF 51 certified as a product class. Stone itself is food-safe (inert mineral); the certification framework doesn't apply to unbranded natural materials in the same way.
ubatuba_granite.domestic_manufacturing_notes: Ubatuba is quarried in Brazil. Fabricated domestically by local fabricators, but the material is imported.
ubatuba_granite.repairability_notes: Chips can be filled with color-matched epoxy. Surface can be re-polished by professional stone restoration. Better repairability than quartz — granite's natural variation helps hide repairs. Major cracks are still problematic.
ubatuba_granite.uv_resistance_notes: Natural granite is UV-stable. No resin to degrade. Suitable for outdoor applications. Proven by centuries of exterior use.
ubatuba_granite.certification_count_notes: Natural stone holds no product-level certifications (Greenguard, NSF, HPD, Declare). The material is inert mineral — certifications are a manufactured-product framework. The Natural Stone Institute provides ASTM testing standards but not product-level certifications.
source_urls: ASTM C615 Standard Specification for Granite Dimension Stone
gaps: Verify flexural_strength_psi against NSI lab test data for Ubatuba specifically
Verify exact water_absorption_pct from NSI test reports

white_ice_granite.manufacturer: Natural stone — quarried primarily in Brazil
white_ice_granite.heat_resistance_f_notes: Same as Ubatuba — granite handles high heat. 1200°F practical rating per user specification.
white_ice_granite.mohs_hardness_notes: White Ice granite: Mohs 6-6.5. Lighter granites with more feldspar and less quartz content tend toward the lower end. Using 6 as conservative estimate.
white_ice_granite.water_absorption_pct_notes: White Ice is a lighter granite with higher porosity than dark varieties like Ubatuba. ASTM C97 testing for light granites typically shows 0.20-0.45% water absorption. Using 0.35% — at the higher end but within ASTM C615 max of 0.40%. This higher porosity drives the increased sealer dependence noted in the tier calibration. Some individual slabs may exceed 0.40%.
white_ice_granite.flexural_strength_psi_notes: Light-colored granites tend to have lower flexural strength than dark, dense varieties. White Ice is a medium-to-coarse grained granite — estimated 1,500-2,200 psi. Using 1,800 psi. This is above ASTM C615 minimum (1,500 psi) but at the lower range for granite. Verify against NSI data.
white_ice_granite.impact_resistance_notes: No specific impact testing data for White Ice granite. Standard granite impact performance — can chip at edges, especially with lighter/more porous varieties.
white_ice_granite.warranty_years_notes: Natural stone — no manufacturer warranty. Same as Ubatuba.
white_ice_granite.warranty_transferable_notes: N/A — no standard manufacturer warranty for natural stone.
white_ice_granite.greenguard_gold_notes: Natural granite — not certified. Inert material, no VOC pathway from the stone itself.
white_ice_granite.nsf_51_notes: Natural granite — not NSF 51 certified as a product class.
white_ice_granite.domestic_manufacturing_notes: White Ice granite quarried in Brazil. Fabricated domestically by local fabricators.
white_ice_granite.repairability_notes: Same as Ubatuba — chips can be filled, surface can be re-polished. Natural variation helps conceal repairs.
white_ice_granite.uv_resistance_notes: Natural granite — UV-stable, no resin to degrade.
source_urls: ASTM C615 Standard Specification for Granite Dimension Stone

_spec_adjustment_preview.description: Preview of how these specs would map to the v2 deterministic adjustment system defined in countertops.json

cambria_brittanicca.notes: Heat gets +1 (>=300°F), not +2 (quartz is below 1000°F threshold). Total +7, within cap of ±8.

dekton_aura_15.notes: Heat gets +2 (>=1000°F). Impact gets -2 (CR documented splitting). Net significantly lower than Cambria despite superior material properties.

caesarstone_calacatta_maximus.notes: Similar to Cambria on material specs but loses on transferable warranty and domestic manufacturing.

msi_q_premium_calacatta_arno.notes: Same as Caesarstone on specs. Differentiation comes from tier placement (MSI is lower tier anchor).

ubatuba_granite.notes: Heat +2 (>=1000°F), but flexural strength -1 (<4000 psi). No certs, no warranty bonuses. Natural material baseline.

white_ice_granite.notes: Same as Ubatuba on adjustments. Water absorption at 0.35% is within ASTM spec (0 adj) but borderline. Material class adjustment of -1 for light granite is applied separately.
